data.title: Chancroid — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Chancroid** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. Synonyms and causative organism?**
- Soft chancre, soft sore, ulcus molle
- Haemophilus ducreyi — Gram-negative coccobacillus, arranged in 'school of fish'/'railroad track' chains

**Q2. Incubation period and why more common in men?**
- 3–7 days (short)
- More common in men (male:female up to 10:1) — women may be asymptomatic carriers; sex workers act as reservoir; uncircumcised men at higher risk

**Q3. Describe the classical ulcer.**
- Multiple painful, soft (non-indurated), ragged undermined ulcers with grey-yellow necrotic purulent base that bleeds easily, surrounded by erythema; kissing ulcers from autoinoculation

**Q4. What is chancroidal bubo?**
- Painful, tender, unilateral inguinal lymphadenitis in ~50% that may suppurate and rupture with a single opening (unlike LGV)

**Q5. Clinical variants?**
- Dwarf, giant, follicular, papular (ulcus molle elevatum), transient, phagedenic, serpiginous, mixed chancre (with syphilis)

**Q6. Differential diagnosis?**
- Primary syphilis (painless indurated), genital herpes (grouped vesicles), donovanosis (beefy red painless), LGV (transient ulcer), traumatic ulcer, Behçet, FDE

**Q7. Investigations?**
- Gram stain of ulcer edge (school of fish), culture on enriched GC agar/Mueller–Hinton with haemin and vancomycin (difficult; transport quickly), multiplex PCR (most sensitive), biopsy (three zones: superficial necrosis, middle vascular zone with endothelial proliferation, deep plasma cell/lymphocyte infiltrate)
- Always test for syphilis (DGI, VDRL/TPHA) and HIV

**Q8. Treatment?**
- Azithromycin 1 g single dose, or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose, or ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily × 3 days, or erythromycin 500 mg three times daily × 7 days
- NACO syndromic kit for genital ulcer disease (non-herpetic) — white kit (benzathine penicillin + azithromycin) covers chancroid and syphilis
- Fluctuant bubo: needle aspiration through healthy skin (not incision)

**Q9. Follow-up?**
- Review at 3–7 days — symptoms improve in 3 days and ulcers heal in 1–2 weeks; treat partners within 10 days; re-test HIV/syphilis at 3 months

**Q10. Does chancroid increase HIV risk?**
- Yes — genital ulcer disease increases both acquisition and transmission of HIV several-fold

## Quick spotter facts
- Multiple painful ragged undermined ulcers with unilateral fluctuant bubo — chancroid

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Long case — Chancroid); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.128; NACO STI guidelines. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
